text:
Situation: FDA first posted the methotrexate sodium injection shortage on 2023-03-13 and it remains current as of 2026-10-21. The shortage listing includes Accord Healthcare Inc., Fresenius Kabi USA LLC, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc., Hospira Inc. a Pfizer Company, and Teva Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. Our inventory shows injection 25 mg/mL at Corvale East with 18 vials (5.9 days) and 29 vials (9.3 days), Corvale General with two lots of 36 vials each (11.9 days each), and tablets 2.5 mg across sites ranging from 11.9 to 26.6 days of supply.

Why (FDA record): A plant associated with the shortage received a Warning Letter on 2016-08-25 and its most recent inspection ended 2025-08-01 with a VAI classification. A registered plant for Zydus Lifesciences Limited (FEI 3007938603) was inspected on 2023-03-24 and classified VAI, 11 days after the shortage posting.

Our position: Injection supply is critically low at multiple sites. Tablet supply is adequate for now. Alembic Pharmaceuticals Inc. is not on FDA's shortage list today and is the rule-based best option, though its label names no plant we could place. Four additional suppliers also are not on the shortage list today and similarly lack plant identification on their labels.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to place orders for methotrexate sodium injection from Alembic Pharmaceuticals Inc. (needs: buyer approval).
2. Buyer to qualify Alembic Pharmaceuticals Limited as a secondary injection source (needs: buyer approval).
3. Buyer to qualify Antares Pharma, Inc. as a tertiary injection source (needs: buyer approval).
4. Buyer to qualify Azurity Pharmaceuticals, Inc. as a quaternary injection source (needs: buyer approval).
5. Buyer to qualify Eugia US LLC as a quinary injection source (needs: buyer approval).
6. Buyer to monitor tablet inventory weekly and report any drop below 14 days at any site (needs: buyer approval).
7. Pharmacy director to review and approve any new supplier agreements before first shipment (needs: pharmacy director approval).

Not recommended: Do not allocate remaining injection stock to non-oncology indications without committee review. Do not initiate therapeutic alternatives or dose changes; those are clinical decisions for the treating clinicians and the committee.
